Hacking the Think Tank II · FAI/IFP · Washington DC

Model choice moves the forecast more than the bill does.

A one-day, pre-registered audit of bill-conditioned forecasting: five enacted laws with frozen first-print ground truth, roughly 7,000 scored runs — holding each bill fixed and varying only the scaffolding nobody reports.

· PolicyEngine × Thesis Institute hackathon · every design committed to git before its first model call

01 · The question

Teams everywhere are building bill → forecast tools. Nobody — including us, until this morning — measures the plumbing.

Feed a statute to a model, get a number for what it will do to enrollment or poverty. The number gets quoted; the model tier, the elicitation format, the pipeline, whether the model saw the bill text or a summary — the harness — does not. We spent the day measuring how much of the answer lives in the harness, on questions where the truth is already printed.

9 events
enacted laws and programs with first-print ground truth — 5 scored below; 4 new bill types in a confirmation sweep, landing (08)
~6,000
scored runs across 28 held-out units + 12 corpus-A units + 14 tool-verified household cases
100%
of pre-registered designs committed to git before their first run — initial registration 09:59 EDT; exploratory probes labeled as such
0
configurations recommended. The dispersion is the deliverable; an adversarial audit of our own statistics is applied throughout

Corpus A is SNAP participation under Pub. L. 118-5 §§311–314: 6 states × 2 target months, forecast from the series as published 2023-06, scored on first prints (CRPS + interval coverage). Unparseable responses stay in the denominators.

02 · Finding 1

Scaffolding moves the forecast by multiples of its run-to-run noise.

Same bill, same data vintage, same question. Below is one real unit from the sweep — Florida SNAP, December-2023 target — with its actual measured cell medians. Flip one dial and watch the forecast move.

Live cell medians · FL · target 2023-12 · 5 repeats per cell

One dial at a time, deliberately: the sweep varies each dimension against a frozen reference (sonnet-5 · operative sections · point+CI JSON); off-axis combinations were not run, and this page does not invent them. The forecaster saw the series as published 2023-06 (last value 3,334,019); the first print, resolved later, is 3,004,132. This unit's measured spreads — model 13.0%, elicitation 11.8%, bill-context 3.6% — sit near the cross-unit medians below. Source: dispersion.md, N=2,520 corpus-A runs.

All five dimensions below: 12 units, 5 repeats per cell, N=2,520 scored runs; spread is the cross-level range of cell medians as a share of the unconditioned median; ratios carry 95% bootstrap CIs over units.

Model tier
9.3% spread · 12.4× its permutation null
Dispersion ratio 4.65 [2.11, 6.46]; survives Bonferroni correction and state clustering. The most defensible number in the study.
Elicitation format
8.1% spread · 4.8× its null
Dispersion ratio 1.73 [1.17, 2.92]; fragile to state clustering (clustered CI spans 1) — suggestive.
Bill context shown
3.5% spread · 4.1× its null (p<0.0003)
Dispersion ratio 1.81 [1.11, 2.65]; carried by the named purpose clause (next chip). Statutory-text-only levels alone are null.
Purpose clause, statute named
−2.65% median shift · p=0.002 · 12 units
A clause with zero mechanical content moved forecasts down in 10 of 12 units (two unmoved; sign test on the 10 nonzero units, p=0.002) — more than the operative sections did (−0.69%). Redact the statute's name and the shift collapses to −0.35% (p=0.29); see 04.
Debate pipeline
~null for magnitude · ratio 0.35 [0.10, 0.76]
No magnitude effect; debate does shift forecasts up in 8/9 moving units (p=0.039) and inflates within-cell variance 5.4×.
Statutory magnitude
null ratio 0.97 · 11 units
A 40-year rewrite of the ABAWD age caps does not move the forecast. That failure is Finding 3.
03 · Finding 2

At default reasoning effort, bill text narrowed the intervals and worsened their coverage.

Showing the model the statute did one thing reliably: it tightened the intervals, while the share of intervals containing the truth fell. The scope clause matters — the interaction with reasoning effort is section 08.

Mean 80% interval, corpus-A reference arm · 60 runs per level
first print
0.50
measured coverage — share of runs whose 80% interval contains the first print (nominal 0.80)
309k
mean 80%-interval width, persons
12/12
units where bill text narrowed the interval (p=0.0005)

Widths and coverage are measured (no-text arm 309k / 0.50; with-text pools the four shown-context arms, 0.33 — the operative-text arm alone is 234k / 0.32). The bar's position against the print is schematic; the coverage numbers are not. No bill-context level improved CRPS over the unconditioned baseline — all four point estimates worse, every CI spans zero.

Out of sample, default effort · N=28 units
Δ +0.047 nCRPS, fable-5 with bill text vs without
At default effort, bill text made fable-5 worse (nCRPS 0.292 → 0.339; coverage 0.66 → 0.61) and bought opus-5 nothing (0.253 → 0.261, coverage flat). The same recipe at max reasoning effort flips sign — the interaction is section 08.
Accuracy, same arm · 12 units
no CRPS gain from any context level
No bill-context level improved CRPS over the no-text baseline (60 runs per level): all four point estimates worse, every CI spans zero. The narrowing above is added confidence without added information.
04 · Finding 3

Forecasts track the statute only where there is nothing to remember.

The standing objection to any backtest is that the model has read the answers. We tested it causally: take one real statute (the $300/week FPUC unemployment supplement), rewrite the dollar amount to $100 / $300 / $900, and move only the target period.

Jan 2021 · standard elicitation
0/3 cells monotone in dose
The period sits inside training data. Forecasts hug the realized trajectory (first print 570.6 — $B at a seasonally adjusted annual rate, BEA W825RC1) at every dose; opus-5 at low reasoning effort returns 570.
Jan 2021 · max reasoning effort
0/4 effort levels break the anchor · 240 runs
At max effort opus-5 spends ~4,400 thinking tokens arriving at the same remembered number. Compute does not substitute for structure.
Jan 2021 · directed derivation
3/3 cells monotone in dose
Direct the model to derive the number step by step and dose-tracking returns even on the memorized period. The binding failure sits in the default elicitation; the capability is present (below).
Nov 2026 · nothing to remember
6/6 cells monotone · spread 2.3–47× repeat noise
Same statute, same doses, operative window moved to Sept–Dec 2026. With no realized trajectory to recall, every cell tracks the dose. (The future arm is never scored; the measurand is dose-response.)
What derivation looks like when it happens — fable-5, future arm, $300 dose (UI outlays, $B at a seasonally adjusted annual rate)
# statute (rewritten): "$300/week supplement · Sept–Dec 2026"
read supplement = $300/wk
estimate weekly claimants ≈ 2.0M
compute 300 × 2.0M × 52 ≈ $31B annualized
compose baseline 36 + 31 = 67 ← its forecast
verify doses $100/$300/$900 → contributions 9.9 / 31.2 / 84.2 ≈ 1 : 3 : 9
The model can do this. On a memorized period, by default, it doesn't.

The decomposition behind 02's purpose-clause chip, run as its own registered design (N=12 units per arm): shown only the clause with the statute named, forecasts fell −2.65% (down in 10 of 12 units, two unmoved; sign test on the 10 nonzero units, p=0.002); name redacted, −0.35% (p=0.29); with "this is the complete bill" asserted, 0.00%; and an access-expanding synthetic clause failed to push forecasts up. The name does the work — the model prices in what it remembers Pub. L. 118-5 doing. At statute scale, the same signature: 6/12 corpus-A units returned identical forecasts under 20-year-stricter and 20-year-looser rewrites of the age caps, both displaced from the unmodified statute.

05 · Finding 4

The tool closes the tier gap on arithmetic; extraction still fails on incomplete text.

The mechanical leg, as a control: S.3596 (the team's demo bill — the CTC phase-in threshold moves from $2,500 to $1) against 14 PolicyEngine-verified household cases. Exact answers, ±$1; single pass; unparseable responses count as wrong; n=70 per cell.

Exact-answer rate, full bill text

The tool converts every model to 100% — haiku-4.5 goes 4% → 100%. A multi-agent pipeline (extractor→analyst→critic→judge) does not substitute — it drops sonnet-5 from 66% to 50% tool-free and needs the tool to reach 100%; opus-5 is at 100% either way (n=70 each).

Input framing · sonnet-5, no tools · n=70 per condition
plain-English summary
94%
full bill text
66%
statutory excerpt, incomplete
50%
§2(a) verbatim with the conforming amendment withheld — 30% on partial-delta traps (n=20)

A verbatim-but-incomplete excerpt is worse input than an honest description. The tool repairs the arithmetic and leaves the extraction failure standing: opus-5 with the tool but the incomplete excerpt dips to 86% (n=70) — a correct calculator fed a mis-extracted threshold.

06 · What this means for the product

The legs separate: mechanical in the tool, forecast without bill text, composition explicit.

Findings 1–4 point the same way: models derive mechanics but recall forecasts, and the harness is part of the answer. So separate the legs — and report the config with the number. Click each leg for the evidence.

Leg 1 · Mechanical
Statute → household arithmetic: PolicyEngine, full text, inside the tool
Evidence: 100% for every model with the tool ↓
  • Every model reaches 100% exact answers with the tool; haiku-4.5 goes 4% → 100%.
  • Extraction still binds: tool + incomplete excerpt = 86% (opus-5). Full text in, tool on.
  • Never compute the statutory delta inside the forecast — that is exactly where the model substitutes memory for derivation (Finding 3).
Leg 2 · Forecast
Outcome forecast: frontier tier at max reasoning effort — bill text only with the budget to use it
Evidence: the effort × context interaction ↓
  • The statutory delta never comes from model memory — it enters computed, from the mechanical leg (Leg 1). The forecast leg predicts the series, not the bill.
  • Significantly-best complete arm (N=28 units): fable-5 · bill text · effort=max — nCRPS 0.208, best Winkler score (1.30) at 0.75 coverage; beats persistence −0.118 [−0.211, −0.035] (22/28 units) and its own naive config −0.084 [−0.164, −0.008] (20/28), with wins across all four events.
  • The identical recipe at default effort is among the worst arms (+0.047 vs its naive baseline, coverage 0.61): bill context requires reasoning budget — at low effort it biases, at high effort it pays (08).
  • Model tier is the dominant dial (12.4× its null, 02); Finding 2's harm is the default-effort case.
Leg 3 · Composition
Combine explicitly in the harness; ship the config with the number
Evidence: the harness moves the answer ↓
  • The policy delta enters here from Leg 1's arithmetic rather than from model memory; the composition is auditable instead of buried in a prompt.
  • Scaffolding choices move the forecast by multiples of sampling noise (Finding 1), so an unreported config is an unreported free parameter.
  • Per-config forward lanes (10) make the sensitivity a measured, running quantity rather than a caveat.
07 · Both legs, same bill

The two legs land within a factor of two; the big swings live in the harness.

The team's PR #64 prices S.3596 mechanically on a certified PolicyEngine build. Our conditionals, committed this morning against the lab's already-registered targets (10), ask frontier models what the published Census series will do if the bill passes. Same bill, same day, two legs.

Mechanical leg · PolicyEngine microsimulation · PR #64, certified build
−0.20pp child poverty
17.02% → 16.82% (−1.2% relative) · budgetary impact −$1.83B · gains concentrated at the bottom of the income distribution · PolicyEngine poverty measure, build P, 2026 static
Forecast leg · conditionals on registered targets · medians of 3 repeats
−0.10 to −0.15pp child poverty
opus-5 / fable-5, conditional on enactment, against Census SPM CY2027

Compared in the same units, the forecast leg concedes one-half to three-quarters of the mechanical effect — on measures that are not commensurable (PolicyEngine's poverty measure on the build-P population, 2026 static, against the Census SPM child rate realized in 2027), so the levels should not be over-read in either direction. The large swings in this study live in the harness, not between the legs: hold the models fixed, vary only what they are shown, and the same conditional delta can inflate or vanish on context alone (09) — which is why the mechanical delta is injected from the mechanical leg rather than re-derived inside the forecast. And the composition can only be scored forward: a model that has already priced the policy into its forecast double-counts any mechanical delta composed on top, so no backtest can validate the composition step; it is scored only in the forward program (10).

08 · What moved accuracy

The gains came from tier, effort, and aggregation; the scaffolds bought nothing.

Held-out accuracy, every arm on matched units (N=28 units, four events), with the Winkler interval score alongside nCRPS so no arm wins by trading coverage away. One dial separates the significantly-best complete arm from one of the worst — reasoning effort, on the same model, same bill text, same elicitation.

Same recipe — fable-5 · bill text · point+CI — one dial · N=28 units

Bill context requires reasoning budget — at low effort it biases, at high effort it pays. Finding 2 (03) is the default-effort half of this interaction.

Where the gains came from
tier · effort · aggregation
Model tier (12.4× its null, 02); reasoning effort (above); and median-of-k aggregation, improving monotonically 0.243 → 0.231 for k=1→5 (N=28 units).
Where they did not
every scaffold tested
Instruction styles (premortem, reference-class, quantiles), debate (02), and scenario/auditor/persona scaffolds cluster at or below the plain arms on matched units (all n.s.; opus-5 at max effort, n=26–28) — and the multi-agent CTC pipeline dropped sonnet-5 from 66% to 50% tool-free (05). The only collaborators that paid were a calculator and a better question.
Cross-type confirmation · N=36 · confirmed
N≈36 units 9 events · 8 bill types
Appropriations, business-side tariffs, an administrative sunset, and a retroactive tax parameter join the corpus (ACP program-creation, scored for dose-response only). Confirmed: on the pooled 36 units the headline arm beats its naive same-model configuration −0.094 [−0.174, −0.022] (26/36 units) and persistence −0.518 [−0.863, −0.228] (29/36); it is near-exact on the advance-CTC pulse (nCRPS 0.08) and best-or-tied on tariffs and the loan restart. The pooled persistence margin is flattered by the new units’ catastrophic mechanical baselines — which is the point: statutory staircases are where extrapolation fails and text-informed forecasting earns its keep. New-type arms ran on a second API transport (recorded per run).
09 · Robustness

The registered number under sixteen harnesses.

Finding 1, pointed at the day's own headline number: the S.3596 deltas recorded this morning (registration pending merge), then run again under 4 bill-context conditions × 2 elicitations × 2 models — 16 configurations, medians of 3 repeats per cell (one cell n=2).

Child-poverty delta, pp · 16 configurations
14/16 configs: −0.10 to −0.30pp
name-only context · fable-5 · −1.5pp (10× the band)
name-only context · 0.00pp

Both configurations outside the band are the name-only context — the model shown the bill's name with no text. That is the channel the purpose-clause decomposition isolated (02, 04): where actual bill text is present, any of it, the recorded delta holds; where only the name is, the delta can inflate ten-fold or vanish.

Qualifying-children delta, M · 16 configurations
16/16 configs positive: +0.3 to +1.2M
0

The behavioral-uptake claim is sign-stable in every configuration. Its magnitude varies 4× across harnesses — which is the number the per-config lanes (10) will score. Values here are the 16-configuration sweep; the reference-config deltas in 10 carry their own labels.

Robustness where the text is present; a disclosure argument where only the name is.

10 · The forward program

Forecasts that cannot be remembered.

Every retrospective accuracy number above sits inside model training windows — Finding 3 is the reason to distrust them, ours included. So the architecture gets applied to the team's own demo bill and recorded against targets with no realized values: S.3596 conditional forecasts on two already-registered ledger targets with first-print resolution rules, runs committed with timestamps — claimed-time chronology from git history, upgraded to the witness-verified tier when the recorder workflow runs on merge (RFC-3161 seal; one command, listed in forward/FORWARD-S3596.md).

SPM child poverty rate, 2027
census.spm.child_poverty_rate.2027
opus-513.60%→13.50%−0.10pp
fable-513.30%→13.15%−0.15pp
current law → S.3596 enacted · medians of 3 repeats
Mechanical channel

Refundable dollars reaching families below the current phase-in floor — the bill's direct channel, composed from the PolicyEngine leg.

Registered target · resolves 2028-08-31
CTC qualifying children, TY2026
irs.soi.ctc.qualifying_children.ty2026
opus-549.3M→49.5M+0.2M
fable-548.5M→48.9M+0.3M
current law → S.3596 enacted · medians of 3 repeats. Δ = median of within-run deltas (fable per-rep +0.4/+0.3/+0.2), which differs from the difference of the scenario medians shown.
Behavioral-uptake claim — the mechanical Δ is zero

A phase-in threshold change does not alter qualifying-child status, so the mechanical answer is zero; the models' +0.2–0.3M asserts filing induced by newly positive credits. The two targets thereby separate the operational effect from the inferred behavioral one — the product's own three-output distinction, applied to its demo bill. If uptake is a fiction, this row gets scored for it.

And the harness becomes a live experiment
per-config lanes prepared
16 near-resolving program-level targets selected for per-configuration forecast lanes; 4 lanes × 3 reps complete on the first four targets, the rest queued. Registration = merge + recorder seal, pending. Finding 1 then re-measures itself — out of training distribution, under the lab's chronology verification, scored mechanically as targets resolve (first resolutions from August 2026; the S.3596 targets in 2028). From here on, the study measures itself.
11 · Read this before quoting anything above

N-statements and honesty notes

  1. N. The 12 corpus-A units are 6 states × 2 months of one program under one law — not independent; the held-out evaluation is N=28 units across four events (the cross-type confirmation at ~36 units is running and not reported here); the corpus-A grid ran at one reference configuration, so its interactions are unmeasured — the one interaction reported (08) was measured directly, out of sample; no claim generalizes beyond the programs tested. State N. Always.
  2. Retrospective accuracy is recall-contaminated by construction (04), ours included — upper bounds, all of it. The forward program (09–10) is the uncontaminated version.
  3. Chronology and audit. Every pre-registered design was committed to git before its first run (initial registration 09:59 EDT, f95c4b6c); first prints were frozen before any model ran; an adversarial audit of our own statistics is applied throughout; held-out comparisons quote the pinned canonical batch (CHECK2.md); all instrument defects found during the day were quarantined, corrected, and are documented in the repository.
  4. PolicyEngine is the reference implementation of the statutory arithmetic — a model input, never ground truth for behavior — and nothing on this page recommends a configuration; where a "best measured arm" is named it is a comparison inside this study.
